# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished 2D underwater exploration/survival web game called **DEEP OCEAN** in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`, with swimming, oxygen, resources, creature AI, treasure, upgrades, zones, lighting/bubbles, HUD, mobile controls and saves.

## Requirements
- Smooth underwater swimming.
- Oxygen management.
- Resource collection.
- Different sea creatures with AI.
- Treasure hunting.
- Submarine upgrades.
- Multiple ocean zones.
- Beautiful underwater lighting and bubbles.
- Health and oxygen indicators.
- Mobile controls and save progress.
- Working exploration and survival mechanics.
- Attachment reference: `https://omgithub.com/api/issue-attachments/e03a5268-8a6d-4203-bb2a-1263469cd4ef` — a cinematic underwater canyon with a small yellow submarine, jellyfish, coral, ruins and god rays.

## Decisions
- Use vanilla static HTML/CSS/ES modules + Canvas 2D; no `package.json` so the platform runtime serves `index.html` directly.
- Self-hosted fonts: Cinzel for titles, Manrope for UI.
- Big procedural world with four depth zones, hand-framed spawn canyon, generated reefs, landmarks and creatures.
- Title screen has a button whose visible label is exactly `Start` so the capture script auto-starts it.
- Save key: `deepocean.save.v1`; autosave and pagehide/visibility saving.
- Renderer split into modules to avoid huge single-file output limits.
- HUD is DOM/CSS; canvas handles the world.
- Current defaults: salvage start 40, 7 chests, 4 zones, pressure ratings 480/900/1400/2100 m.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` created with full HUD, title, fabricator, pause, game-over, victory overlays, SVG icon sprite and accessible controls.
- `css/style.css` created: glass HUD, responsive mobile layout, upgrade grid, title treatment, animations, vignette/grain.
- `js/utils.js`: math, seeded RNG, color helpers, formatting.
- `js/save.js`: schema normalization, load/write/clear, defaults.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio ocean ambience, bubbles, sonar, pickups, damage, whale calls, mute.
- `js/world.js`: zones/palettes, chests, upgrades, pressure/depth helpers, procedural reefs/resources/creatures/ambient jellies.
- `js/renderer.js`: core water, surface, canyon walls, distant ridges, whale silhouette, god rays, motes, decor dispatch, bubbles, particles, sonar pulse, fronds, vignette/damage effects.
- `js/render-environment.js`: reefs, kelp, coral, vents, beacon, chests, resources.
- `js/render-ruins.js`: columns, arch, slab, wreck, vault, temple, bones, archive, ruin growth.
- `js/render-creatures.js`: fish schools, jellyfish, sharks, anglerfish, mantas, stun visuals.
- `js/render-player.js`: yellow submarine with dome, propeller, fins, lights, claw, damage smoke and headlight cone.
- `js/hud.js`: HUD sync, toasts, zone banners, fabricator rendering/purchases, joystick and button wiring, overlays.
- Font files and OFL licenses downloaded under `assets/fonts/`.

### Active
- `js/game.js` is **not yet written**; core simulation, input, lifecycle, autosave, creature AI, collecting, interaction, pressure, death/victory, camera and main loop still needed.
- `js/main.js` is **not yet written**; game bootstrap/export still needed.
- No testing, browser screenshots or visual iteration has happened yet.

### Blocked
- None technically, but existing modules reference missing game fields/APIs and will fail until `game.js`/`main.js` exist.

## Next Move
1. Write `js/game.js` implementing the Game class and all mechanics/state/input/UI calls expected by existing modules.
2. Write `js/main.js` to instantiate the game, resize the renderer, run the RAF loop and expose a debug handle.
3. Start the static server and capture with Playwright; fix runtime errors.
4. Inspect desktop and mobile screenshots, then iterate on visual quality and gameplay issues.
5. Verify title auto-start, chest opening, upgrades, oxygen/pressure death, saves and touch joystick.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: missing central simulation/lifecycle/input module — highest priority.
- `js/hud.js`: defines required Game methods/fields (`startGame`, `newExpedition`, `pauseGame`, `resumeGame`, `openFabricator`, `closeFabricator`, `buyUpgrade`, `repairHull`, `triggerSonar`, `setBoost`, `setJoystick`, `interact`, `respawn`, `returnToTitle`, `continueExploring`, `saveGame`, `toggleMute`; fields `player`, `salvage`, `relics`, `openedChests`, `stats`, `currentZone`, `pressureOver`, `sonarCooldown`, `sonarMax`, `mode`, `muted`, `upgrades`).
- `js/renderer.js`: renderer expects `game.time`, `game.camera`, `game.mode`, `game.titleSub`, `game.player`, `game.chests`, `game.resources`, `game.creatures`, `game.world`, `game.bubbles`, `game.particles`, `game.pulse`, `game.damageFlash`, `game.pressureOver`.
- `js/render-player.js`: expects player fields `x/y/vx/vy/facing/speed/health/healthMax/oxygen/oxygenMax/lightsOn/lampScale/invulnerable/boosting`.
- `js/render-creatures.js`: creature fields include `type/x/y/size/color/phase/dir/angle/state/stun/hazard/fish/flee`.
- `js/world.js`: exports `WORLD`, `ZONES`, `CHESTS`, `TOTAL_CHESTS`, `UPGRADES`, `upgradesAt`, `zoneAt`, `zoneIndex`, `depthAt`, `createWorld`.
- `js/hud.js`, `js/save.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/utils.js`: supporting modules already complete.
- `index.html`, `css/style.css`: UI structure/styling already complete.
- `assets/fonts/`: Cinzel/Manrope woff2 + OFL licenses.
- `$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs`: static server behavior; serves project root when `index.html` exists.
- `$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/capture-start.mjs`: auto-clicks only buttons whose trimmed label matches `/^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i`.

## Important Context
- No `package.json` allowed unless adding proper Vite config; plain static HTML is the intended path.
- The game must be served with `./start.sh` (uses `RUNTIME_DIR`; defaults to port 3000 unless `PORT` set). Agents notes mention `http://localhost:3002` for Pascal, but capture script uses `APP_PORT`/3000 defaults.
- `capture.sh` captures desktop `1440x900` and mobile `390x844` into `$CAPTURE_DIR`, auto-clicks Start, waits 1s, screenshots.
- Screen capture auto-start only works while Start button label is exactly `Start`; do not change it to “Continue”.
- Renderer `zoom` mobile logic is `clamp(W/560, .62, .9)`; desktop `clamp(min(W/1360,H/800), .7, 1.06)`.
- `world.js` currently includes a duplicate `forbidden` chest coordinate `{x:1845,y:1410}` but harmless.
- `render-environment.js` imports `drawRuin` from `render-ruins.js` and re-exports it; renderer imports `drawRuin` via environment.
- Title start flow must hide `#title-screen` with `.gone`, remove `.is-hidden` from `#hud`, set `mode='playing'`, init/resume audio, and sync HUD.
- Saving should persist upgrades, salvage, relics, opened chest IDs, discovered zones, collected non-oxygen resource IDs, player position/health/oxygen/facing, stats, completed, muted, timestamps.
- Oxygen pickups should respawn (e.g. 25s) and not be persisted as permanently collected; other resources one-time.
- Pressure damage should trigger when `depthAt(player.y) > player.ratedDepth`, with HUD warning and death handling.
- Startup/title rendering must show the rich spawn canyon; `createWorld()` spawn is `(1220, 1200)`.
- No tests or screenshots exist yet; likely many integration bugs to resolve once game.js is added.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished 2D underwater exploration/survival web game called **DEEP OCEAN** in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`, with swimming, oxygen, resources, creature AI, treasure, upgrades, zones, lighting/bubbles, HUD, mobile controls and saves.

## Requirements
- Smooth underwater swimming.
- Oxygen management.
- Resource collection.
- Different sea creatures with AI.
- Treasure hunting.
- Submarine upgrades.
- Multiple ocean zones.
- Beautiful underwater lighting and bubbles.
- Health and oxygen indicators.
- Mobile controls and save progress.
- Working exploration and survival mechanics.
- Attachment reference: `https://omgithub.com/api/issue-attachments/e03a5268-8a6d-4203-bb2a-1263469cd4ef` — a cinematic underwater canyon with a small yellow submarine, jellyfish, coral, ruins and god rays.

## Decisions
- Use vanilla static HTML/CSS/ES modules + Canvas 2D; no `package.json` so the platform runtime serves `index.html` directly.
- Self-hosted fonts: Cinzel for titles, Manrope for UI.
- Big procedural world with four depth zones, hand-framed spawn canyon, generated reefs, landmarks and creatures.
- Title screen has a button whose visible label is exactly `Start` so the capture script auto-starts it.
- Save key: `deepocean.save.v1`; autosave every 12s plus `pagehide`/`visibilitychange`.
- Renderer split into modules to avoid huge single-file output limits.
- HUD is DOM/CSS; canvas handles the world.
- Current defaults: salvage start 40, 7 chests, 4 zones, pressure ratings 480/900/1400/2100 m.
- Oxygen drains slower than a simple 100-second timer (`0.4 + depth/1850*0.56 + boost 0.38`); oxygen pickups respawn after 26s.
- Victory triggers after all 7 chests are opened; `continueExploring()` resumes play.
- Title staging places the submarine at the spawn canyon while preserving the saved position in `resumePos` for gameplay resume.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`: full HUD, title, fabricator, pause, game-over, victory overlays, SVG icon sprite and accessible controls.
- `css/style.css`: glass HUD, responsive mobile layout, upgrade grid, title treatment, animations, vignette/grain.
- `js/utils.js`: math, seeded RNG, color helpers, formatting.
- `js/save.js`: schema normalization, load/write/clear, defaults.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio ocean ambience, bubbles, sonar, pickups, damage, whale calls, mute.
- `js/world.js`: zones/palettes, chests, upgrades, pressure/depth helpers, procedural reefs/resources/creatures/ambient jellies.
- `js/renderer.js`: water, surface, canyon walls, distant ridges, whale silhouette, god rays, motes, decor dispatch, bubbles, particles, sonar pulse, fronds, vignette/damage effects.
- `js/render-environment.js`: reefs, kelp, coral, vents, beacon, chests, resources.
- `js/render-ruins.js`: columns, arch, slab, wreck, vault, temple, bones, archive, ruin growth.
- `js/render-creatures.js`: fish schools, jellyfish, sharks, anglerfish, mantas, stun visuals.
- `js/render-player.js`: yellow submarine with dome, propeller, fins, lights, claw, damage smoke and headlight cone.
- `js/hud.js`: HUD sync, toasts, zone banners, fabricator rendering/purchases, joystick and button wiring, overlays.
- Font files and OFL licenses downloaded under `assets/fonts/`.
- `js/game.js`: complete Game class implementing state, save/load, title/start/new expedition, input, movement, collisions, oxygen/pressure/health, resource collection, creature AI, sonar, chest interaction, fabricator upgrades/repair, death/respawn, victory, autosave, camera, particles/bubbles.
- `js/main.js`: renderer/game bootstrap, RAF loop, resize/orientation handlers, `window.deepOcean`/`__DEEP_OCEAN__` debug handles.
- Static server running via `tmux` session `deepocean` on `http://localhost:3000`; `node --check` passed for both new modules.
- Playwright desktop/mobile smoke test passed with zero page errors; auto-click Start reached `mode: "playing"` at spawn `(1220, 1200)`, 82 resources, 72 creatures, 96 colliders, 250 decor.
- Isolated a real render defect: large dark rectangular shapes in the starting view are **not** compositor artifacts; they originate from reef drawing and disappear when reefs are removed. Removal tests for ruins, kelp, coral, vents did not remove them.
- Confirmed there is only one canvas, one `main.js` resource, one RAF loop, one game/renderer instance (`sameWorld: true`, `gameIsGame: true`); no page errors.
- Performance measurement: canvas render ≈10–13 ms, game update <2 ms, but RAF runs at only ~1.3–4 fps under Xvfb/SwiftShader with heavy CSS glass/backdrop effects; canvas `toDataURL` matches page screenshot for normal rendering.
- Debug screenshot files are under `/tmp/opencode/shots/`; scripts under `/tmp/opencode/debug*.mjs` and `/tmp/opencode/capture.mjs`.

### Active
- Visual debugging of the reef rendering defect causing large dark rectangles in the opening scene.
- A final isolation harness (`/tmp/opencode/debug16.mjs`) was just prepared to test whether the canvas is actually being cleared between frames and inspect pixel colors with a solid red custom render, but it has not yet been executed.

### Blocked
- None technically. The reef artifact is the immediate visual bug; low RAF FPS under software rendering may also need optimization (likely reduce/disable expensive CSS `backdrop-filter`/overlay animation in capture environment).

## Next Move
1. Run `/tmp/opencode/debug16.mjs` and inspect whether `ctx.getImageData` and `toDataURL` show solid red, confirming whether the canvas clears correctly.
2. Fix `js/render-environment.js` `drawReef`/`blobPath` so reef lumps render as intended organic silhouettes instead of tall dark rectangles; compare against `/tmp/opencode/shots/scene-canvas.png` and `without-reef.png`.
3. Re-capture desktop `1440x900` and mobile `390x844`, then iterate on visual quality, camera framing, seaweed density and scene composition.
4. Investigate/optimize the ~1.3–4 fps RAF rate under SwiftShader; consider reducing costly `backdrop-filter` blur, animated grain/scan overlays, and excessive decor detail.
5. Exercise gameplay: movement/boost, resource pickup, oxygen respawn, sonar, chest opening, fabricator purchases/repair, pressure death/respawn, victory, pause/return-to-title, save persistence and mobile joystick.
6. Verify the official capture flow (`capture.sh`/`default-capture.mjs`) auto-starts via the exact `Start` label and produces clean screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: central Game implementation; all simulation/lifecycle/input/save logic now lives here.
- `js/render-environment.js`: contains `drawReef`/`blobPath` usage implicated in the large dark rectangle artifact; fix priority.
- `js/renderer.js`: render order and culling; drawDecor calls environment renderers; includes water/canyon/rays/particles.
- `js/world.js`: `createWorld()`, `CHESTS`, zones, resource and creature spawn data, reef/collider generation.
- `js/hud.js`: required Game API and HUD/overlay methods; DOM sync.
- `js/main.js`: bootstrap/RAF loop/debug globals.
- `js/save.js`: save normalization and `deepocean.save.v1`.
- `js/render-player.js`: submarine/headlight visuals and expected player fields.
- `js/render-creatures.js`: creature visuals and expected creature fields.
- `js/render-ruins.js`: ruins/landmark drawing; ruled out for current rectangle artifact.
- `index.html`: DOM IDs/overlays/HUD and module entry.
- `css/style.css`: HUD/title/mobile layout; heavy glass/backdrop effects may contribute to low software FPS.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/`: desktop/mobile and debug screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/debug16.mjs`: pending canvas-clear isolation test.

## Important Context
- Static server: `tmux` session `deepocean`, `PORT=3000 ./start.sh`, URL `http://localhost:3000/`.
- Capture auto-start matches buttons whose trimmed label is exactly `/^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i`; keep the title button label `Start`.
- Capture uses Playwright headed Chromium under Xvfb with SwiftShader; low frame rate is a software-rendering artifact, but visual defects still matter.
- Large dark rectangles are drawn into the canvas (confirmed via `toDataURL`), correlate with reefs, and vanish when `game.world.decor` has reefs filtered out.
- Initial camera at `(1220, 1180)`; spawn `(1220, 1200)`; depth HUD shows 300 m; pressure default 480 m.
- `game.creatures` is a mapped copy of `world.creatures`; clearing `world.creatures` does not remove rendered creatures—use `game.creatures`.
- The custom render isolation attempts initially appeared to show stale full scenes because their clear pass did not reset `globalCompositeOperation`/`globalAlpha`; debug16 addresses this.
- `renderer.render()` resets `globalAlpha=1` and `globalCompositeOperation='source-over'` at frame start.
- HUD `sync()` writes DOM every ~0.08s; objective updates every ~0.7s; autosave every 12s.
- Save excludes oxygen pickup permanence; only non-oxygen resources are recorded in `collected`.
- No git commit/push has been made for the new `game.js`/`main.js` work.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

That will make bar-chart read as coral fan.

Real organ pipe coral looks exactly like that, so it's plausible. The dark mouths help. It's okay, though the teal ones look like UI equalizers. Adding a base mound helps.

ctx.fillStyle = rgba(mixColor(color, '#031015', 0.55), 0.9);
ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(0, 2, count*3.9, 4, 0, 0, TAU); ctx.fill();
